content.text:
Editing what is on the page (change only what they asked for; check the rest still holds):
- A part of the effect bigger / smaller / denser / faster / another colour -> set_part(id, size=..., amount=..., speed=..., colour=...); "remove the X" when X is a part -> remove_part(id); "add X" -> add_part when a part fits.
- "make it pop" -> more contrast, not more stuff: a brighter core or flash on the peak frame, a crisper edge (lower soft), a ramp with a lighter top.
- "less busy" -> fewer particles, calmer noise (lower erosion/octaves), remove a secondary layer; keep the silhouette.
- "slower" / "faster" -> {"op": "retime", "frames": N} keeps the duration (fps follows) and puts every life window on a frame; or change fps alone. "loop every N frames" -> retime frames N.
- "a wind-up before it" -> {"op": "retime", "lead_in": k} adds k frames before everything (one-shots).
- "half the size" / "bigger" -> {"op": "scale", "factor": 0.5} scales positions, radii, widths, speeds and the sliders that write them about the origin (the sprite keeps its size); then render with fit_canvas=true.
- "face left" / "the other way" -> "mirror": "x" (set it with a patch): the whole effect flips, the sprite keeps its own pixels.
- "remove the X" / "undo the X" -> remove_layer (its sliders go with it), or remove_group: give layers that belong together a "group" name when you add them, so they can go together later.
- "match my character's colours" -> a ramp built from the sprite's colours in the first message (dark -> light).
- "a slider for X" -> add_control; for an animated value bind it with "mode": "mul".
- If they name something the sprite should have (a sword, a staff) and the sprite in the first message doesn't show it, say so instead of inventing where it is.

patch = list of ops applied in order to your working recipe ([] renders it as is): {"op": "set", "path": "layers.circle.radius", "value": 40} (any path: layers.<id>.<field>[.from|.keys.1.1], controls.<id>.value, camera.tilt, ramps.main, frames ...); {"op": "remove", "path": "layers.sparks.wobble"}; {"op": "add_layer", "layer": {...}, "after": "<id>"} (or "before"; default: on top); {"op": "replace_layer", "layer": {...}}; {"op": "remove_layer", "id": "<id>"}; {"op": "add_control", "control": {...}}; {"op": "replace_control", "control": {...}}; {"op": "remove_control", "id": "<id>"}; {"op": "remove_group", "group": "<name>"} (every layer with that group, and their sliders); {"op": "retime", "frames": N, "keep": "duration"|"speed"} (duration: fps follows; life windows land on frames) or {"op": "retime", "lead_in": k} (k frames before everything, one-shots); {"op": "scale", "factor": 0.5, "about": [x, y]} (positions, radii, widths, speeds and their sliders; about defaults to the origin; the sprite keeps its size); {"op": "move", "group": "<name>", "by": [dx, dy]} (a group's positions and the sliders that write them). A set on a value a control writes moves that control instead.

---
Other topics: start, parts, recipe, craft, cookbook, presets, tools, tool <name>

review before your next call: say what you see in the frames — does it read at 1x, start -> peak -> end (or a loop with no jump), anything cut off at the edges, muddy colours, is the sprite still readable — then choose: set_part or render with a patch (a defect you saw), get_part (unsure what a part can do), or export. Put that reasoning in `notes`.
